threads.title: East Maui water
threads.whereItStands: The court-ordered contested-case hearing on the permits that let Mahi Pono and East Maui Irrigation divert East Maui streams was postponed from November 4 to January 19, 2027, to allow more time for evidence and witnesses. Separately, after six months of talks ended without agreement in June, the East Maui Water Authority says it will gradually take over the ditch system, while Mahi Pono wants to remain its long-term operator.

updates.headline: Contested-case hearings on East Maui water diversion start November 4
updates.summary: Court-ordered contested-case hearings over Mahi Pono and East Maui Irrigation's stream diversion permits begin November 4th and will run like a trial.
updates.text: The fight over East Maui water is moving into a new legal phase. The East Maui Regional The Community Board was told Friday of court ordered contested case hearings over Mauhi Pono and East Maui irrigation's permits to divert water from East Maui streams. The hearings start November 4th with additional hearings November 5th and again on December 1st. The proceeding will operate much like a trial with sworn testimony and cross-examination

updates.headline: Judge orders contested case hearing on East Maui stream diversions
updates.summary: A judge ordered a contested case hearing on a temporary permit for East Maui stream diversions, letting groups challenge whether the land board protected Native Hawaiian practices and the public trust.
updates.text: A judge has ordered a contested case hearing over a permit allowing continued diversion of water from East Maui streams. The hearing will allow parties, including the Sierra Club of Hawaiʻi and Namokuʻaupuniʻokoʻoʻolauhui, to challenge the state's decision to issue a temporary permit authorizing water diversions. The dispute centers on whether the Board of And the natural resources adequately protected Native Hawaiian practices, stream restoration efforts, and the public trust before approving the permit. The ruling has broad implications for the long-term management of the island's freshwater resources.

updates.headline: East Maui water talks fail between Water Authority and Mahi Pono
updates.summary: After six months of talks ended without agreement, the East Maui Water Authority says it will gradually take over the ditch system while Mahi Pono wants to remain long-term operator.
updates.text: The future of East Maui's historic irrigation system could soon return to the spotlight. After a six-month effort to reach a compromise between the East Maui Water Authority and Mahipono ended without an agreement. According to Civil Beat, the Water Authority says it's prepared to gradually take over management of the century-old gravity-fed ditch system, while Mahipono wants to remain the state's long-term operator under its own management

updates.headline: Water board hears East Maui update, pauses Hana Ranch system purchase
updates.summary: The Board of Water Supply heard from the East Maui Regional Community Board, and the department paused plans to acquire the Hana Ranch water system.
updates.text: The Maui Board of Water Supply received an update from the East Maui Regional Community Board, which continues to pursue the issue of clean water. Mahipono maintains that it owns the entire system and is not interested in selling or co-managing. Separately, the Department of Water Supply reported it has paused plans to acquire the Hana Ranch water system after concluding the proposed purchase terms were not in the county's best interest.

updates.headline: Mahi Pono and county clash over East Maui streams
updates.summary: A standoff over control of East Maui's streams continues between Mahi Pono and the county, with state officials yet to decide on a lease, a shift to the county, or a contested case.
updates.text: A standoff continues over control of East Maui streams with Mahi Pono The state officials have yet to decide whether to grant a long-term lease or shift control to the county or force a contested case. The county argues public control would improve water security and stewardship, while Mahipono questions whether the county is ready to take over. With no compromise on the table, the dispute The investigation is now heading towards legal and administrative decisions in the months ahead.

updates.headline: East Maui residents urge county takeover of water system
updates.summary: At a state Senate hearing, residents and officials pushed for Maui County to manage East Maui's largest water system and warned against private and foreign control of water.
updates.text: State senators got an earful about East Maui water yesterday, with residents and officials pushing for Maui County to take over management of the island's largest water system. They Arguing it conflicts with public trust and local values. The hearing exposed a deep divide between state-level decision-making and Maui's long-term vision for local control over land and water resources. Some say this is yet another example of state government disregard for the wishes of Maui citizens.

updates.headline: East Maui Water Authority holds public meeting in Keʻanae
updates.summary: The county invites the public to a 4 p.m. Friday, September 26th meeting at Keʻanae Uka covering grants, community feedback, testimony and operations.
updates.text: The county is inviting the public to the East Maui Water Authority meeting beginning at 4 p.m. Friday, September 26th, at Kāenaeʻuuka, which is at 13375 Hāna Highway. They will share grant opportunities, recap June community feedback from Kāenae, Kula, and Haʻikū, take testimony, and give an operations update. Water is life.

updates.headline: Hawaii Supreme Court rules against BLNR on East Maui streams
updates.summary: The Hawaii Supreme Court ruled the Board of Land and Natural Resources violated water advocates' constitutional rights by letting Alexander & Baldwin drain East Maui streams without a full hearing.
updates.text: The Hawaii Supreme Court ruled that the State Board of Land and Natural Resources violated the constitutional rights of water advocates by allowing Alexander in Baldwin to drain East Maui streams without providing water to the people of the island.

updates.headline: OHA trustee says Maui County should own East Maui Irrigation system
updates.summary: OHA trustee Carmen Lindsey said the county, not Mahi Pono, should own the East Maui Irrigation system, while Mahi Pono says the ownership change won't affect operations.
updates.text: OHA Trustee Carmen Lindsey said Maui County should own the East Maui irrigation system to ensure fair water distribution, not mahipono. Her comments follow my response. Mahipono's full acquisition of the system from A&B, which has diverted water for over 150 years. Lindsey noted that the system is in poor condition and will require funding for repairs. Mahipono stated the ownership change will not affect operations and will continue supplying water to upcountry Maui and supporting agriculture. Akakū filmed those recent East Maui Water meetings, incidentally, and they are being replayed on Akakū Channel 53 and available on the playlist on our free app, Maui Stream.

updates.headline: Mahi Pono takes full ownership of East Maui Irrigation
updates.summary: Mahi Pono took full ownership of East Maui Irrigation after Alexander & Baldwin transferred its 50% stake and waived a $2.7 million payment.
updates.text: Mahipono has taken full ownership of East Maui irrigation after reaching an agreement The system was in agreement with Alexander and Baldwin on June 17. A&B transferred its 50% stake and waived the $2.7 million payment initially agreed upon. Mahipono will now manage the system to support its agricultural operations. The East Maui irrigation system has diverted East Maui stream water for nearly 150 years. A&B is shifting focus to its agricultural system. The companies cited diverging missions as the reason for this split.

updates.headline: East Maui kalo farmers face water threats despite returned streams
updates.summary: Since water was returned to East Maui streams in 2018, kalo farmers face changing rainfall, drought and invasive species that leave them less water than expected.
updates.text: In 2018, a historic decision by the State Water Commission forced diverted water to be returned to East Maui streams, enabling farmers to grow kalo once again. But now they're They are up against other threats like changing rainfall, persistent drought and invasive species. All are taking a toll on the watershed and leaving farmers with less water than expected from those streams.

updates.headline: East Maui Water Authority plans free water planning events
updates.summary: The East Maui Water Authority and ʻAha Wai o Maui Hikina invite the public to free events June 16 to 18 on watershed planning and water use.
updates.text: Water is life, and it's worth finding out more about life. The East Maui Water Authority and ʻAho Vai o Maui Hikina invite the public to free water resource planning events, June 16th through the 18th. These include a field trip to K&I, a public finance panel, and community meetings in Kula, Haʻikū, and Hoelo. Topics will focus on watershed planning and water use. For meeting details, contact EM Water Authority at co.maui.hi.us.
